questions.question: Pipes A and B together can fill a tank in 10 hours. Pipes B and C together can fill the same tank in 12 hours. Pipes A and C together can fill the same tank in 15 hours. In how many hours can pipe B alone fill the same tank?
questions.solution:
**Given**

A and B together can fill a tank in 10 hours

B and C together can fill the same tank in 12 hours

A and C together can fill the same tank in 15 hours

**Formula used:**

For combined work, 1/(time of work) equals to sum of rates of work

**Solution:**

⇒ 1/A + 1/B = 1/10

⇒ 1/B + 1/C = 1/12

⇒ 1/A + 1/C = 1/15

⇒ Adding all three equations we get 2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15

⇒ From which we get 1/B = 2/(1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15) - 1/10 - 1/15

**Therefore, the time taken by pipe B alone to fill the tank is 120/7 hours **

questions.question: Two inlet pipes can separately fill a cistern completely in 8 hours and 10 hours, respectively. They are operated for 2 hours, after which the second pipe is closed, and an outlet pipe which can drain out water from the full cistern in 20 hours is opened. How much time will it take to fill the cistern completely from the instant of opening the outlet pipe?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two inlet pipes can separately fill a cistern completely in 8 hours and 10 hours, respectively. They are operated for 2 hours, after which the second pipe is closed, and an outlet pipe which can drain out water from the full cistern in 20 hours is opened. 

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency (Work done per hour) × Total time taken 

1 hour = 60 minutes

Calculation:

LCM (8, 10) = 40

Let the capacity of the tank be the LCM of 8, 10.

Hence, the capacity of the tank = 40 units

Efficiencies (per hour),

First pipe = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 units

Second pipe = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 units

Outlet pipe = 40 ÷ 20 = 2 units

In first two hours, tank was filled by = 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 units

Remaining = 40 - 18 = 22 units

Here, the efficiency is taken negative since it's draining the water outside. 

Then, taken taken to fill the tank = 22 over (5 - 2) = 71 over 3 hours = 7 hours 20 minutes 

**∴ It will take to fill the cistern completely from the instant of opening the outlet pipe 7 hours 20 minutes.**

∴ Tank will be completely filled in 120/13 minutes = 9(3)/({13)} minutes

questions.question: An inlet pipe A originating from a river can fill a reservoir in 30 days. And an outlet pipe B, which is capable of emptying the completely filled reservoir in 50 days, drains out the water from the reservoir to an irrigation canal. The pipes are opened on alternate days starting with A. On which day form the beginning will the reservoir get completely filled for the first time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A can fill in 30 days and pipe B can empty it in 50 days

Pipes are open in an alternate day starting with A

**Concept Used:**

LCM of individual time = Total work

Once the reservoir is filled, work done by the outlet pipe can't be calculated.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/679b514e72ff09c96919bccfc401021173cf00860462ca5a94ec36beb450bc78.png] 

Let total work = 150 unit,

When the reservoir will completely fill, last work will be done by pipe A

And the filling was started with pipe A, so in odd days pipe A will open and in even days pipe B will open

Pipe A works on first day, and on the next day pipe B works,

Reservoir fill by Pipe A and pipe B in 2 days = 5 – 3 = 2 unit.

⇒ 146 units reservoir will fill by both pipe in 146 days

In 147th days pipe A will open again and it will fill (146 + 4) = 150 units

**∴ In 147th day from the beginning, the reservoir get completely filled for the first time.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] **

Many times we calculate (5 - 3) = 2 unit filled in 2 days

⇒ in 1 day filled 1 unit

⇒ A total of 150 units will be filled in 150 days. 

But this is wrong.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] 

Many times we consider in the last day it will be completely filled by pipe A and subtract the efficiency of pipe A from total capacity and calculate accordingly. 

But by this, we will get the remaining part = (150 - 5) = 145 unit which will fill by pipe A and pipe B

⇒ It means on the 145th day pipe B was open, but as starts with pipe A, on odd days pipe A will be open. (1st, 3rd, 5th, .... days)

So, this will lead us to the wrong answer.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 10 h, Pipe B can fill the same tank, when empty, in 15 h, and Pipe C can empty the same tank, when completely full, in 12 h. Find the time taken to fill half the tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 10 h, Pipe B can fill the same tank, when empty, in 15 h, and Pipe C can empty the same tank, when completely full, in 12 h.

**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency × time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10, 15, and 12 is 60 units which can be assumed as the total capacity of the tank.

Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 10 h.

The efficiency of Pipe A = 60/10 = 6 units/h

Pipe B can fill the same tank, when empty, in 15 h.

The efficiency of Pipe B = 60/15 = 4 units/h

Pipe C can empty the same tank, when completely full, in 12 h.

The efficiency of Pipe C = - 60/12 = - 5 units/h [Here negative sign represents that the pipe is used to empty the tank.]

Time is taken to fill half the tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty = {(60)/(2)} over (6+4-5)

⇒ {30} over (5) = 6 hours

**∴ The time taken to fill half the tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty is 6 h.**

questions.question: Pipe V1 can fill an empty tank in 8 hours. Pipe V2 can fill the same tank in 16 hours. Pipe V3 can empty the same, completely filled, tank in 12 hours. If three pipes are opened simultaneously, then in how much time will the tank get completely filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe V1 can fill an empty tank in 8 hours.

Pipe V2 can fill the same tank in 16 hours.

Pipe V3 can empty the same completely filled tank in 12 hours.

Three pipes are opened simultaneously.

Formula used:

For LCM method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another fills the same tank in 'b' hours and a third one empties the full tank in 'c' hours and all of them are opened together, then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by three different pipes = LCM of (a, b, c)

Efficiency of first pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/a

Efficiency of second pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/b

Efficiency of third pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/c

Combined efficiency of them = (+ efficiency of 1st pipe) + (+ efficiency of 2nd pipe) + (- efficiency of 3rd pipe)

[(+ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which fills the tank and (-ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which empties the tank.]

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

For Alternate method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another fills the same tank in 'b' hours and a third one empties the full tank in 'c' hours and all of them are opened together, the net part filled in 1 hour = 1/a + 1/b - 1/c

∴ Time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a + 1/b - 1/c) = abc/(bc + ac - ab) hours

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0aea245b2b7472a0ca677825d546513b76d745cb40de2410b9b49ca9fbc43a81.png] 

In fig, LCM of (8, 16, 12) = 48 = Total work

Efficiency of V1 = 48/8 = 6

Efficiency of V2 = 48/16 = 3

Efficiency of V3 = 48/12 = 4

Combined efficiency = (+ 6) + (+ 3) + (- 4) = 5

**∴ If all three pipes open simultaneously, then the tank filled in = 48/5 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png] 

V1 fills in 8 hours

V2 fills in 16 hours

V3 empties in 12 hours

So time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a + 1/b - 1/c) = 1/(1/8 + 1/16 - 1/12) = 1/(5/48) = 48/5 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 48/5 hours. **

questions.question: Pipes P and Q can fill a completely empty tank in 24 minutes and in 36 minutes, respectively, when opened independently. Pipe R can empty the completely filled tank in 30 minutes. Initially all the three pipes P, Q and R, are opened simultaneously. After how many minutes should pipe Q be closed so that the tank is filled in 1 hour?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe P to fill a tank = 24 min

Time taken by Pipe Q to fill a tank = 36 min

Time taken by Pipe R to fill a tank = 30 min

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

1 hour = 60 min

**Calculation:**

LCM of 24, 36 and 30 is 360

Let the height of the tank is 360m.

Efficiency of Pipe P = (360/24) = 15 i.e Pipe P can fill the tank at a rate of 15m/min

similarly,

Efficiency of Q = (360/36) = 10m/miin

Efficiency of R = (360/30) = 12m/min (rate of emptying the tank)

Now,

Let Pipe Q closed after x min

According to the question,

Pipe P will work for 60 min

Pipe Q will work for x min

Pipe R will work for 60 min

⇒ (15 × 60) + (10 × x) – (12 × 60) = 360

⇒ 900 + 10x – 720 = 360

⇒ 180 + 10x = 360

⇒ 10x = 180

⇒ x = 18 min

**∴ The required time is 18 min**

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

Now, if another pipe fills the tank in 'c' hours, then

Combined efficiency of the three pipes = (- efficiency of pipe A) + (- efficiency of pipe B) + (+ efficiency of pipe C)

(-)ve sign is mentioned as they empty the tank and (+)ve sign is to imply that the pipe fills the tank.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/716db7cfaeda1353ddfb5f5d9a747cb22febeba60c0c3f5c1f3475bcc2842393.png] 

Here in the fig, LCM of (8, 12) = 24 = Total work 

Efficiency of A = 24/8 = 3

Efficiency of B = 24/12 = 2

(-)ve sign is mentioned as A and B empty the tank.

1/6th of total work = 24/6 = 4 = combined efficiency of three pipes

Let the efficiency of pipe C be x, then

⇒ x – 3 – 2 = – 4

⇒ x = 5 – 4

⇒ x = 1

**∴ the pipe C alone can fill the tank in = 24/1 = 24 hrs**

questions.question: An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 2 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 3 hours. In what time will the empty tank get filled, if the inlet and the outlet pipes are opened together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 2 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 3 hours. 

Formula used:

For LCM method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and they are opened together, then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by two pipes = LCM of (a, b)

Efficiency of first pipe = LCM of (a, b)/a

Efficiency of second pipe = LCM of (a, b)/b

Combined efficiency of them = (+ efficiency of 1st pipe) + (- efficiency of 2nd pipe)

[(+ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which fills the tank and (-ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which empties the tank.]

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

For Alternate method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and they are opened together, the net part filled in 1 hour = 1/a - 1/b

∴ Time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a - 1/b) = ab/(b - a) hours

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afe3a7cac67016cac84cbc6210b8342eef010913fa029eb008940cd2a0e492a4.png] 

In fig, LCM of (2, 3) = Total work = 6

Efficiency of Inlet pipe = + 6/2 = + 3

Efficiency of Outlet pipe = - 6/3 = - 2

Combined efficiency = 3 - 2 = 1

If both pipes open together, then the tank filled in = 6/1 = 6 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4dc8c3e83508eaf43bce3e473329500aa0b5140181df4d5d2a28e24bd3c31c58.png] 

Inlet pipe fills in 2 hours

Outlet pipe empties in 3 hours

So time taken to fill the tank = (2 × 3)/(3 - 2) = 6 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 6 hours.**

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours. Due to the leak in its bottom, the tank is filled in 12 hours. If the tank is full, then that leak can empty the tank in how many hours?

Detailed solution:

Let the hours taken by the leak to empty a full tank be x.

⇒ Part of tank emptied in 1 hour = 1/x

Part of tank filled in 1 hour without leak = 1/10

Part of tank filled in 1 hour with leak = 1/12

⇒ 1/10 – 1/x = 1/12

⇒ 1/x = 1/10 – 1/12 = 1/60

∴ Leak will empty a full tank in 60 hours.
